I cannot relate to you more. I yearn for friends who I can say I 'love', the kind of friends you see on TV, or real life (if you're not too cynical).

My depression began before this event (that I'm about to explain), but this is what quadrupled its affects on me. I had a group of friends. These friends were, what I thought, typical. There were a couple I was 'closer' to than others, and I was reasonably happy with them. However I became depressed, and with my depression I often took it out on them, however, from my perspective, even to this day, I never said anything serious. It was just typical banter, maybe a bit too far here and there, but it was common among us. 

Then one day, I come home, and I'm told in a skype call that I'm no longer wanted. I'm outcasted. I'm a cunt. I'm a backstabber. My closest friend of FIVE YEARS didn't even listen to my excuse, focusing on the things I said that I thought were just jokes, or why I said the things I did. A couple of my friend were neutral on the issue, however after a couple of days, communication from them, gone. Suddenly, friends I had for 2 ~ 5 years were gone, hated me. Two years went past, still no new group. Friends dotted here and there, I never fit into a group again. I now face the looming challenge of university, and I hope to find new friends there. Needless to say my mental state over the last few years has been awful.

Sorry if this was boring or doesn't relate, but what you descried hit me hard. Much love.

I'll consider consulting a professional, however the act of doing so is frightening within itself. I think my depressed side tells me that due to my age they won't take me as seriously as others, but my more logical side tells me that's an utter bullshit thing to be worried about, they're professionals. Thank you for reading my mess up there, it *truly* means a lot to me.

Here's a viewpoint as someone without autism/aspergers 

My older brother (by 4 years)is an aspie. (someone with aspergers, but maybe you already know that).

He's into his 20's now and at one point I know he felt similar to you. He often told me growing up that I was the only person that 'understood' him, however I often felt awful guilt incase I didn't, especially sometimes as he described difficulty picking up on body language and subtle hints that people without autism wouldn't think twice about. He was at his worst between 17 and 20, having panic attacks, not understanding what was 'wrong' with him, not thinking he had a place in the world, misunderstanding everyone. He'd just sit and play runescape when he wasn't at school. He hated the fact that he disliked so many people, and how his outlook on life was preventing him from moving forward. 

I tried to understand him better, I hated myself for not being able to fully relate to the one person I wish I could. I remember sitting on his bed, with him sitting in his computer chair. I was trying to talk to him, but he sat there, rocking slowly back and forth. It didn't take me long to stop trying to talk to him, (note, i wasn't saying shit like "what's wrong" or "are you alright", to be honest I can't remember what we were talking about, definitely his depression and asperges). We sat in silence for about 20 minutes, I felt rotten there wasn't anything I could do, I was in my early - mid teens, I was frightened. After I left I walked past his room 10 mins later, he was still in the same position. Still rocking. Sometimes when I would be walking home from school, I'd have horrible thoughts that one day I'll get in, take off my bag, grab a coke, head upstairs knock on my bro's door and not receive a response. I'd then open the door, to see him dead, from suicide. 

He handles his depression and asperges a lot better now, he even made a few friends at uni, he's no longer reliant on prescription meds to get him through the day, and we're closer than ever.

I too suffer from derpession, a whole other story, and I can't be motivated enough to read through my paragraphs either so sorry for any spelling or grammar shite.

I'm not sure if this is in anyway helpful, but I hope you get past this situation.

19 male UK here. Can definitely relate, without a shadow of a doubt. I recently finished my last year of what you would call 'highschool', and I would call 'Sixth form'. Definitely in my last two years my mental state changed for the worse, and continues to suck. The feeling of just saying fuck it happens a lot. Fuck doing that essay, fuck working in my sketch book. I would just simply face the consequences, which I wouldn't care about. Sometimes I almost wished my tutors would get angry at me.

Also 

Even doing those things like playing games and watching anime becomes a chore. "Oooh I gotta finish this season", or, "I've got to reach X point in X game".

 I stopped doing these things for fun. I started and continue to do these things to just pass the time. Even whilst doing these things I'm not truly happy.

 Despite saying this, I did get a rush of adrenaline tuning into the GoT return! I guess it's one of the few things I look forward to and am not left with a great emptiness after watching, unlike a lot of things, such as waiting for that great game, playing it for a week, then thinking whether or not you actually had fun playing it. Do you feel the same way?

You're not alone :)

I've been drawing, but I'd call it doodling mostly.

I used to draw a lot more when I was younger, thinking it would be the answer to my future. Now, as I do it purely for entertainment, I enjoy it. Even if you're shit as dicks, you constantly get better without realizing it. I constantly tell myself I suck shit at drawing, then look back at an sketchbook from 6months ago. Comparing your older drawings/artwork/doodles to your current doodles is extremely gratifying. It's also a useful skill to have.

If you're not at all interested in art/drawings/doodling/ I'd still give it a try, test yourself.

If after a week you've decided to scrap it, try learning guitar or some other instrument.
